# FOR002 `loop-order-not-column-major`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

The innermost loop runs over a non-leading array dimension while an outer loop runs over the leading one.

## Why

Fortran stores arrays column-major: `a(i, j)` and `a(i+1, j)` are adjacent in memory, `a(i, j)` and
`a(i, j+1)` are a whole column apart. The innermost loop must run over the leftmost subscript to
walk memory with stride 1; the swapped order makes every access a cache miss and stops
vectorisation. Reported when, for most array references of the innermost loop, its index is in a
later dimension and the enclosing loop's index in the first.

## Reported

```fortran
do i = 1, ni
  do j = 1, nj
    a(i, j) = b(i, j) + c(i, j)
  end do
end do
```

## Preferred

```fortran
do j = 1, nj
  do i = 1, ni
    a(i, j) = b(i, j) + c(i, j)
  end do
end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[FOR002] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = FOR002` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
